nodes.description: Proteomic profiling of Ube3c-deficient mouse forebrain and human brain organoids identifies CBLL1 (Hakai) as a UBE3C substrate. Loss of UBE3C stabilizes CBLL1, and the UBE3C-CBLL1 pair sets the level of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) mRNA methylation; in UBE3C-deficient neural progenitors the m6A writers are hyperactivated. Disease-associated UBE3C mutations also alter the ligase's autoubiquitination. This arm is EMERGING and rests entirely on model systems reported in a preprint.

In Ube3c-deficient murine cortex and human iPSC-derived brain organoids, loss of UBE3C shifts the cellular composition of the cortex, favoring neurogenesis and suppressing glial fate, with neural progenitors failing to exit the cell cycle normally. The defect is reversible in vivo in mouse by the METTL3 inhibitor STM2457, which is a preclinical proof of mechanism and not a treatment.

nodes.description: UBE3C ubiquitinates substrates that are already partially threaded into the proteasome, committing them to complete proteolysis. When UBE3C is absent or catalytically dead, or cannot bind the proteasome, stable substrates are degraded slowly and incompletely and are released as truncated fragments; cells become more vulnerable to proteotoxic stress. UBE3C is also the ligase that clears low-burden misfolded, oligomer-enriched species in mammalian cells.

nodes.description: UBE3C is a HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase that binds the 19S regulatory particle of the 26S proteasome through its N-terminal domain and assembles Lys29- and Lys48-linked polyubiquitin chains through its C-terminal HECT domain. It cycles on and off the proteasome together with the deubiquitinase USP14, with substrate load driving the association. Biallelic loss of UBE3C removes this activity from the particle.

Neurons are long-lived and post-mitotic and cannot dilute damaged proteins by division, so they are the cell type in which a chronic reduction in proteasomal processivity is expected to be limiting. The HECT-type UBE3 ligase family as a whole is required for cortical circuit assembly and higher cognitive function, which is the general reason a ligase-family defect presents as a neurodevelopmental syndrome. The specific neuronal consequence of UBE3C loss in human brain has not been measured, and this node is the inferential link in the canonical chain.

nodes.description: NOT A TREATMENT FOR PATIENTS. STM2457 is a small-molecule METTL3 (m6A writer) inhibitor. It is curated here solely because it is the one intervention shown to act on this disorder's proposed mechanism: in Ube3c-deficient mice it reverses the neural progenitor cell-cycle-exit defect in vivo. It has never been given to a person with NEDSMB, the mechanism it targets is the EMERGING epitranscriptomic hypothesis rather than established disease biology, and the supporting report is a preprint. It is recorded as a target_mechanisms lead so the pathograph carries the therapeutic hypothesis explicitly, and must not be read as a therapy recommendation.
